findings.description: Both vault-tls/ and nginx-tls/ directories are empty but mounted read-only in docker-compose. Nginx config expects certs at /etc/nginx/tls/fullchain.pem and privkey.pem. Vault config has tls_disable=true but TLS certs are mounted.
findings.rationale: Production TLS certificates are completely missing. Nginx will fail to start without valid certs. Vault TLS is disabled but certs exist in mount config - inconsistent state.

findings.description: Vault healthcheck uses 'vault status -tls-skip-verify' which bypasses TLS certificate validation.
findings.rationale: TLS verification explicitly disabled in healthcheck. This defeats the purpose of TLS and allows MITM attacks on Vault communications.

findings.description: .gitignore does not ignore secrets/ directory - only ignores .vault-token. Plaintext secret files exist in secrets/ directory (postgres_password.txt, redis_password.txt, vault_token.txt, API keys).
findings.rationale: Secrets directory is not gitignored. All production secrets stored as plaintext files in repo. These will be committed if not careful. Also .env.example exists which may reference these.

findings.description: Docker Compose defines secrets using 'file:' pointing to plaintext files in secrets/ directory instead of using Docker secrets or external secret managers.
findings.rationale: File-based secrets in compose work for local dev but are not production-ready. Should use Docker secrets (swarm) or external secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.) before production deploy.

findings.description: Postgres (5432), Redis (6379), Vault (8200/8201), API (3000/9090), Prometheus (9091), Grafana (3001), Alertmanager (9093) all expose ports to host (0.0.0.0). Only Nginx 80/443 should be exposed.
findings.rationale: Internal services should not be accessible from host network. This is a configuration issue - remove 'ports:' for internal services, use internal network communication only. Nginx 80/443 exposure is correct for ingress.

findings.description: CSP header includes 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' for script-src, and 'unsafe-inline' for style-src. This weakens XSS protection significantly.
findings.rationale: Production CSP should not allow unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval. Need to use nonces/hashes or remove inline scripts/styles. Can fix before deploy without blocking Block 4.

findings.description: Vault UI enabled (ui=true) and exposed on port 8200 to host network. No IP restrictions on Vault listener (0.0.0.0:8200).
findings.rationale: Vault UI should not be exposed publicly in production. Should bind to internal network only or add auth proxy. Config change needed before production.

findings.description: Vault audit log file mode set to 0644 (world-readable). Audit logs contain sensitive access information.
findings.rationale: Audit logs should be 0600 or 0640 at most. World-readable audit logs leak security events. Simple config fix before deploy.

findings.description: Vault listener has tls_disable=true but Vault address configured as https://vault:8200. Inconsistent TLS configuration.
findings.rationale: Vault is configured to use HTTPS addresses but TLS is disabled. Must enable TLS with valid certs or use HTTP consistently. Config fix needed.

findings.description: Empty TLS directories with ro mounts mean self-signed certs would be used in production if any certs were present. Combined with -tls-skip-verify, this creates false sense of security.
findings.rationale: The entire TLS setup is non-functional for production. Self-signed certs with skip-verify defeats TLS guarantees. Must have valid CA-signed certs and proper verification before Block 4 passes.

findings.description: Grafana admin password uses Docker secret (good) but GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER is hardcoded as 'admin' in compose.
findings.rationale: Admin username is not secret; password is properly secret-managed. Username 'admin' is common but not a security issue by itself.

findings.description: API service exposes port 9090 (metrics) to host in addition to 3000. Nginx restricts /metrics to RFC1918 IPs but direct API port bypasses this.
findings.rationale: Metrics endpoint exposed directly on API port 9090 bypasses Nginx IP restrictions. Should remove 9090 from ports or bind to localhost only.
